title: Double Chocolate Glazed Cake Doughnuts
summary: Tender cocoa cake doughnuts made with Greek yoghurt, fried and dipped in a glossy dark chocolate glaze.
equipment: 8 cm doughnut cutter (or 8 cm and 2.5 cm round cutters)
large heavy pan or casserole, at least 24 cm wide
wire rack over a tray lined with kitchen paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

ingredients.note: check the label; many contain soya lecithin or traces of milk

steps.title: Mix the dry
steps.text: Whisk the flour, cocoa, baking powder, bicarbonate and salt together in a bowl.

steps.title: Mix the wet
steps.text: In the second bowl whisk the sugar and eggs for about 1 min until a little thickened, then whisk in the yoghurt, cooled butter and vanilla.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Fold the dry ingredients into the wet with a spatula just until no dry streaks remain. The dough will be soft; cover it and chill for 1 h until it firms up.

steps.title: Roll and cut
steps.text: Roll the dough 1.2 cm thick on a well-floured surface and stamp out rings, dipping the cutter in flour each time. Re-roll the scraps once to get 12 rings and their holes, lay them on the floured tray and chill for 20 min.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Fill the pan with oil to about 4 cm, no more than half full, and heat it to 180 °C.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Fry 3 rings at a time for 60-75 seconds a side at 175-180 °C. They are done when they float high, the cracks look dry and a cocktail stick pushed into the side comes out clean; the holes need about 45 seconds a side. Drain on the rack and cool for 10 min.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Melt the chocolate into the hot milk in the heatproof bowl, then whisk in the icing sugar, cocoa and vanilla until smooth and shiny. Dip the top of each doughnut, let the extra drip back and leave for 15 min to set.

tips: The most common mistake is adding too much flour while rolling; use it on the surface and cutter, not worked into the dough, or the doughnuts turn dry.
Cocoa dough looks done before it is, so trust the cocktail stick, not the colour.
Keep the oil at 175-180 °C; cooler oil makes greasy doughnuts.
Warm the glaze for a few seconds if it thickens while dipping.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best on the day. Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days.
